translation_en: Musaddad narrated to us; Yahya ibn Said narrated to us, from Ubaydullah, who said: Nafi narrated to me, from Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “A Muslim must listen and obey in what he likes and dislikes, unless he is commanded to commit a sin. If he is commanded to commit a sin, then there is no listening and no obedience.”

Umar ibn Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us; my father narrated to us; al-Amash narrated to us; Sad ibn Ubaydah narrated to us, from Abu Abd al-Rahman, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, sent out a military detachment and appointed a man from the Ansar as their commander, ordering them to obey him. The commander became angry with them and said: “Did the Prophet not command you to obey me?” They said: “Indeed.” He said: “I firmly command you to gather firewood, light a fire, and enter it.” They gathered firewood and lit a fire. When they were about to enter it, they looked at one another and said: “We only followed the Prophet to escape the Fire.” They remained that way until the fire died down and the commander's anger subsided. When they returned, they mentioned it to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. He said: “If they had entered it, they would never have come out of it. Obedience is only in what is right.”

Hajjaj ibn Minhal narrated to us; Jarir ibn Hazim narrated to us, from al-Hasan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Samurah, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Abd al-Rahman, do not ask for authority. If you are given it because you asked for it, you will be left to manage it alone; but if you are given it without asking, you will be helped in it. If you take an oath and then see that something else is better, expiate your oath and do what is better.”

Abu Mamar narrated to us; Abd al-Warith narrated to us; Yunus narrated to us, from al-Hasan, who said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Samurah narrated to me: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to me: “Abd al-Rahman ibn Samurah, do not ask for authority. If you are given it because you asked, you will be left to manage it alone; if you are given it without asking, you will be helped in it. If you swear an oath and then see that something else is better, do what is better and expiate your oath.”

Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us; Ibn Abi Dhib narrated to us, from Said al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurairah, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “You will be eager for authority, and it will be a cause of regret on the Day of Resurrection. How excellent it is at first, and how evil it is when it ends.” Muhammad ibn Bashshar said: Abdullah ibn Humran narrated to us; Abd al-Hamid narrated to us, from Said al-Maqburi, from Umar ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Hurairah, who said this.

Muhammad ibn al-Ala narrated to us; Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Burayd, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I entered upon the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, with two men from my people. One of them said: “Appoint us, Messenger of Allah.” The other said the same. He replied: “We do not appoint to this position anyone who asks for it or is eager for it.”

Abu Nuaim narrated to us; Abu al-Ashhab narrated to us, from al-Hasan: Ubaydullah ibn Ziyad visited Maqil ibn Yasar during the illness in which he died. Maqil said to him: I will tell you a hadith I heard from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. I heard the Prophet say: “There is no servant whom Allah entrusts with the care of people who fails to look after them sincerely, except that he will not find the fragrance of Paradise.”

Ishaq ibn Mansur informed us; Husayn al-Jufi informed us. Zaidah said: Hisham mentioned it, from al-Hasan, who said: We visited Maqil ibn Yasar while he was ill. Ubaydullah entered, and Maqil said to him: I will tell you a hadith I heard from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. He said: “No governor who is placed in charge of a Muslim community and dies while betraying them will be forbidden Paradise.”

Ishaq al-Wasiti narrated to us; Khalid narrated to us, from al-Jurayri, from Tarif Abu Tamimah, who said: I was present with Safwan, Jundab, and their companions while he was advising them. They asked: “Did you hear anything from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him?” He said: I heard him say: “Whoever seeks to be heard by people, Allah will expose him on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever makes things difficult for others, Allah will make things difficult for him on the Day of Resurrection.” They said: “Advise us.” He said: “The first part of a person to rot is his stomach. So whoever can eat only what is good, let him do so. Whoever can ensure that nothing comes between him and Paradise but a handful of blood he has shed, let him do so.”

Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us; Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Salim ibn Abi al-Jad, who said: Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us: While the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and I were leaving the mosque, a man met us near the mosque's entrance and asked: “Messenger of Allah, when is the Hour?” The Prophet said: “What have you prepared for it?” The man seemed subdued, then said: “Messenger of Allah, I have not prepared much prayer, fasting, or charity for it, but I love Allah and His Messenger.” He said: “You will be with those you love.”

Ishaq narrated to us; Abd al-Samad informed us; Shu'bah narrated to us; Thabit al-Bunani narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik, who said to a woman from his family: “Do you know so-and-so?” She said: “Yes.” He said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, passed by her while she was weeping at a grave and said: “Fear Allah and be patient.” She said: “Leave me alone; you have not suffered my loss.” He went on. A man later passed by her and asked: “What did the Messenger of Allah say to you?” She said: “I did not recognize him.” He said: “He was the Messenger of Allah.” She went to the Prophet's door and found no doorkeeper there. She said: “Messenger of Allah, I did not recognize you.” He said: “Patience is only at the first shock.”

Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Dhuhli narrated to us; al-Ansari Muhammad ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from Thumamah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: Qays ibn Sad used to stand before the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, in the position of a police officer before a ruler.

Musaddad narrated to us; Yahya narrated to us, from Qurrah, who said: Humayd ibn Hilal narrated to me; Abu Burdah narrated to us, from Abu Musa: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, sent me out and sent Muadh after me.

Abdullah ibn al-Sabbah narrated to me; Mahbub ibn al-Hasan narrated to us; Khalid narrated to us, from Humayd ibn Hilal, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa: A man had accepted Islam and then become a Jew. Muadh ibn Jabal came while he was with Abu Musa and asked: “What is this?” He said: “He accepted Islam and then became a Jew.” Muadh said: “I will not sit down until I kill him. This is the judgment of Allah and His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him.”

Adam narrated to us; Shu'bah narrated to us; Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr narrated to us: I heard Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakrah say: Abu Bakrah wrote to his son, who was in Sijistan: “Do not judge between two people while you are angry, for I heard the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, say: ‘No judge should rule between two people while he is angry.’”

Muhammad ibn Muqatil informed us; Abdullah informed us; Ismail ibn Abi Khalid informed us, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, from Abu Masud al-Ansari, who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and said: “Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I am late for the dawn prayer because so-and-so makes it too long for us.” I had never seen the Prophet more angry in an admonition than he was that day. Then he said: “People, some of you drive others away. Whoever among you leads the people in prayer should keep it short, for among them are the weak, the elderly, and those who have needs.”

Muhammad ibn Abi Yaqoub al-Kirmani narrated to us; Hassan ibn Ibrahim narrated to us; Yunus narrated to us. Muhammad said: Salim informed me that Abdullah ibn Umar informed him that he had divorced his wife while she was menstruating. Umar mentioned this to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and the Messenger of Allah became angry. Then he said: “Tell him to take her back and keep her until she becomes pure, then menstruates and becomes pure again. If he then decides to divorce her, he may divorce her.”

Abu al-Yaman informed us; Shuayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Urwah told me that Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: Hind bint Utbah ibn Rabiah came and said: “Messenger of Allah, by Allah, no household on earth was more beloved to me to see humiliated than your household; and today no household on earth is more beloved to me to see honored than yours.” Then she said: “Abu Sufyan is a miserly man. Would I be at fault if I fed those dependent on him from his property?” He said: “Feed them what is reasonable.”

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to me; Ghundar narrated to us; Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: I heard Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, intended to write to the Romans, they said: “They do not read a letter unless it is sealed.” So the Prophet had a silver ring made. I can almost see its gleam; its inscription read: “Muhammad, Messenger of Allah.”

Abu al-Yaman informed us; Shuayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: al-Saib ibn Yazid, the son of Nimir's sister, informed me that Huwaytib ibn Abd al-Uzza told him that Abdullah ibn al-Sadi told him: He came to Umar during his caliphate, and Umar said to him: “Was I not told that you take on public duties, but when you are given payment for the work you dislike it?” I said: “Yes.” Umar said: “What do you want from it?” I said: “I have horses and servants, and I am well off. I want my work to be charity for the Muslims.” Umar said: “Do not do that. Do not ask for authority, for if you are appointed because you asked, you will be left to manage it alone. If you are appointed without asking, you will be helped in it.”

Al-Zuhri said: Salim ibn Abdullah narrated to me that Abdullah ibn Umar said: I heard Umar say: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, used to give me a gift, and I would say: “Give it to someone poorer than me.” He once gave me money, and I said: “Give it to someone who needs it more than I do.” The Prophet said: “Take it, keep it, or give it in charity. Whatever of this wealth comes to you without your coveting it or asking for it, accept it; but do not pursue what does not come to you.”
Ali ibn Abdullah narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us. Al-Zuhri said: Sahl ibn Sad said: I witnessed the two spouses who invoked mutual curses, and I was fifteen years old when they were separated.

Yahya narrated to us; Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us; Ibn Jurayj informed us; Ibn Shihab informed me, from Sahl, a man of Banu Saidah: A man from the Ansar came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and said: “What do you think if a man finds another man with his wife? Should he kill him?” The two spouses then invoked mutual curses in the mosque, and I was present.

Yahya ibn Bukayr narrated to us; al-Layth narrated to me, from Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Salamah and Said ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurairah, who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, while he was in the mosque, called out to him, and said: “Messenger of Allah, I have committed adultery.” He turned away from him. When the man had testified against himself four times, he said: “Are you insane?” He said: “No.” He said: “Take him and stone him.”

Ibn Shihab said: Someone who heard Jabir ibn Abdullah informed me that he said: I was among those who stoned him at the prayer ground. Yunus, Mamar, and Ibn Jurayj reported it from al-Zuhri, from Abu Salamah, from Jabir, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, regarding stoning.

Abdullah ibn Maslamah narrated to us, from Malik, from Hisham, from his father, from Zaynab bint Abi Salamah, from Umm Salamah, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “I am only a human being, and you bring your disputes to me. Perhaps one of you is more persuasive in presenting his argument than another, and I judge according to what I hear. If I award someone something that rightfully belongs to his brother, let him not take it, for I am only allotting him a piece of the Fire.”

Qutaybah narrated to us; al-Layth narrated to us, from Yahya, from Umar ibn Kathir, from Abu Muhammad, the freedman of Abu Qatadah, that Abu Qatadah said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said on the day of Hunayn: “Whoever has evidence concerning a person he killed may take that person's belongings.” I stood to find evidence about a man I had killed, but I saw no one who could testify for me, so I sat down. Then I changed my mind and told the Messenger of Allah about it. A man sitting with him said: “The weapon of the man he mentioned is with me.” The Prophet said: “Give it to him.” Abu Bakr said: “No, by Allah, he will not give the spoils of one of Allah's lions to a weakling from Quraysh and thereby strengthen the enemy of Allah and His Messenger.” The Messenger of Allah said: “Give it to him.” So he gave it to me.Abdullah said, reporting from al-Layth: The Prophet stood up and handed it to me. The people of the Hijaz say that a judge does not rule on the basis of his personal knowledge, whether he witnessed the matter during his period of authority or before it. If a litigant admits in the judge’s presence, during a court session, that another person has a right against him, some of them say the judge should not rule against him until he calls two witnesses and they testify that they heard the admission. Some people of Iraq say that a judge may rule on what he heard or saw in court, but if it occurred elsewhere, he should rule only on the testimony of two witnesses. Others among them say that he may rule on it, because he is entrusted with the duty, and testimony is only intended to establish the truth; his own knowledge is greater than testimony. Some say he may rule on the basis of his knowledge concerning property, but not in other matters. Al-Qasim said: A judge should not issue a ruling based on his own knowledge without other evidence, even though his knowledge may be greater than another person’s testimony. Doing so exposes him to suspicion among the Muslims and causes them to fall into doubts. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, disliked suspicion, as shown when he said: “This is Safiyyah.”

Abd al-Aziz ibn Abdullah narrated to us; Ibrahim narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab, from Ali ibn Husayn: Safiyyah bint Huyayy came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. When she left, he walked with her. Two men from the Ansar passed by, and he called them and said: “This is Safiyyah.” They said: “Glory be to Allah!” He said: “Satan flows through the son of Adam like blood.” Shuayb, Ibn Musafir, Ibn Abi Atiq, and Ishaq ibn Yahya also reported it from al-Zuhri, from Ali—from Husayn—from the Prophet.

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us; al-Aqadi narrated to us; Shu'bah narrated to us, from Said ibn Abi Burdah, who said: I heard my father say: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, sent my father and Muadh ibn Jabal to Yemen and said: “Make things easy and do not make them difficult; give good news and do not drive people away; and cooperate with one another.” Abu Musa said to him: “In our land a drink called bit is made.” He said: “Every intoxicant is forbidden.” Al-Nadr, Abu Dawud, Yazid ibn Harun, and Waki also reported it from Shu'bah, from Said, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet.

Musaddad narrated to us; Yahya ibn Said narrated to us, from Sufyan, who said: Mansur narrated to me, from Abu Wail, from Abu Musa, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “Free the captive and accept the invitation.”
